proposal.title: Pelynthra: a funding transparency dashboard for projects
proposal.summary: Pelynthra builds a funding transparency dashboard for projects for maintainers and their funders.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Projects are not able to show funders where their money went. Maintainers and their funders are depending from open source sustainability every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We are going to build a funding transparency dashboard for projects called Pelynthra. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Open source sustainability belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We are maintaining http://forge.test/pelynthra/pelynthra, which 202 public projects depend on. Our team is working on open source sustainability for 4 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/pelynthra/pelynthra. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 10 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 10.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 55200.00 EUR for 94 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Projects are not able to show funders where their money went. Maintainers and their funders are depending from open source sustainability every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We are going to build a funding transparency dashboard for projects called Pelynthra. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Open source sustainability belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We are maintaining http://forge.test/pelynthra/pelynthra, which 202 public projects depend on. Our team is working on open source sustainability for 4 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/pelynthra/pelynthra. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 10 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 10.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 55200.00 EUR for 94 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.
